blocks.x: Cloud, Edge & Platform applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Manufacturing & Industrial, cloud, edge & platform engineering builds the runtime for everything else we do: hybrid and multicloud architecture, cloud-native modernization of legacy estates, edge and distributed infrastructure for latency-critical operations, sre and reliability engineering, internal developer platforms, finops, and mission-critical high-performance systems. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: hybrid & multicloud architecture, cloud-native & legacy modernization, edge computing & distributed infrastructure — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Twinverse with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Energy and OEE economics unmeasured
Energy per unit and OEE components lack trustworthy telemetry, so improvement programs guess. Corporate ESG reporting for plants is a spreadsheet festival.
Brownfield instrumentation gap
Critical assets run uninstrumented because gut-and-replace is unthinkable; the data that twins and models need does not exist, and downtime for retrofit is unaffordable.
Quality escapes and manual inspection

Defect detection depends on sampling and eyes; escapes reach customers, and scrap/rework costs hide in the P&L. Vision systems stall in pilot because lighting, thresholds and line integration were never engineered.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: NIS2 (EU operators) and ISO 9001/IATF 16949 quality systems. Traceability and process control evidence for audits. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
